From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@brightcart.com>

Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: p99 & large latency regressions on /v1/generate since noon PST

Hi Markus / Monica,

We started seeing big p95/p99 jumps in production around 12:10pm PST after what looks like the platform change you deployed (tokenizer/quant-profile flag?).
Symptoms:
- p95 up from ~220ms to ~1.1s; p99 up to 3.8s on our gen endpoint.
- Aggregate tokens/sec dropped on our bins from ~1.6k tok/s -> ~260 tok/s.
- Error rate increased slightly (429 throttles + occasional 500s when long responses).

We attached a perf dump and a short trace from our side (perf_dump_20270920.zip). This is impacting checkout recommendations and causing timeouts for customers. Can you confirm root cause and ETA to fix?

Jordan
Senior SRE, BrightCart

Quick asks:
- Rishi: triage kernel/quant selector change, perf diffs, KV-cache behavior.
- Laura/Sean: propose immediate mitigation (route, rollback, traffic split).
- Monica: own customer comms - short, transparent, ETA.

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 15:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: p99 & large latency regressions on /v1/generate since noon PST

Quick initial triage (prelim, from infra telemetry):
- Change window aligns with rollout of quant-profile selector v2 at 11:58am (feature flag: quant-selector-alpha).
- Observed smaller batch sizes in dispatcher (mean batch size down ~45%) and frequent KV cache evictions on the affected shards. That combination reduces amortized per-token work and increases latency variance.
- Trace snippet: "dispatch: batch_size=3; kv_hit=false; kernel=matmul-fast-16q" vs baseline: "batch_size=12; kv_hit=true; kernel=matmul-fast-8q".
- Tokens/sec for same model config measured by our perf harness fell from ~1700 tok/s -> ~240 tok/s on impacted nodes.

Attaching a small profile excerpt: profile_snippet.txt. I'm running a kernel-level microbench now to confirm whether the new kernel path is regression or protective for memory.
Immediate recommendation: flip quant-selector-alpha to route BrightCart traffic to previous selector and revert the rollout while we root-cause (30-60m).

Rishi
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
[attachment: profile_snippet.txt]
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 16:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: p99 & large latency regressions on /v1/generate since noon PST

Agree with Rishi. Proposed mitigation plan (playbook):
1) Immediate: gate quant-selector-alpha for BrightCart and 5 other high-p99 customers via traffic policy (no deploy) — expected p99 drop to near baseline in ~10-15m after routing stabilizes.
2) If routing doesn't improve within 30m: urgent rollback of selector code from the morning deploy (requires ops window ~45m).
3) Post-mortem: capture perf traces + add a canary perf test for quant selector changes.
4) Customer action: notify BrightCart of temporary traffic routing, provide ETA and credit offer.

I'll create a minimal rollback_playbook.md and coordinate with Ops. Mark, Monica — want to send a short note to Jordan once we flip the gate so they know it's targeted and reversible.

Laura
SRE Lead, Platform Reliability

- If that doesn't restore p99 to acceptable levels, we will roll back the selector from this morning's push (target 45m).

Estimated next update: 30 minutes. Apologies for the disruption — Monica will keep you updated and we'll follow up with a formal incident summary + credit.

Markus Klein

Redwood Inference

Status update: we flipped the routing gate at 16:26 PST (quant-selector -> previous-stable). Early telemetry:
- p95 trending down to ~240-270ms within first 5 minutes; p99 moving towards ~320-420ms.
- Tokens/sec on the affected service moving from ~260 tok/s back to ~1.3k tok/s on canary nodes.
- No new 500s observed; throttles returned to baseline.

We will keep the gate for 2 hours and capture full perf diffs. Next: create regression test that exercises batching under realistic client inter-arrival distributions.

Rishi
